recommendation: Keep the empty audit commit as-is. No core source follow-up is needed for FHIR-44992 unless a later work-group decision creates a broader policy to allow pattern names such as Request as Reference target shorthand in resource definitions.
issue_request: FHIR-44992 was Applied with a Not Persuasive with Modification resolution after PR #3050 failed with "ERROR @ Communication.basedOn: Reference to invalid resource Request". The decision was that Reference(Request) is not appropriate for resource definitions because most elements should enumerate the appropriate current request resources rather than accept every current and future Request-pattern resource.
initial_application: The relevant Communication.basedOn change path started in FHIR-38783: fa35c0d85e changed the target to StructureDefinition/Request, then 525068e04f replaced that target with an explicit concrete-resource list before PR #3050 merged. Later a910985a9b cited FHIR-44992/PR #3050 and applied the same style of correction to ServiceRequest.basedOn after a similar build failure.
additional_context: The Jira-linked Zulip thread records the build failure and the mapping-exception problem: participants initially considered Request shorthand possible, then identified that concrete resource enumerations needed to be recognized as equivalent for mapping purposes. FHIR-I minutes on 2024-04-16 corroborate the Not Persuasive with Modification decision. source/fhir.ini lists Communication and ServiceRequest as active resources, so the inspected StructureDefinition and mapping exception files are in build scope.
reconciliation: No source change was made. Communication.basedOn currently enumerates concrete request resources instead of StructureDefinition/Request, and communication-event-mapping-exceptions.xml records the Request-pattern mismatch with the concrete extra target list. ServiceRequest.basedOn/replaces and their Request mapping exceptions are likewise already enumerated.

related_jiras.note: Its Communication.basedOn Reference(Request) edit in PR #3050 exposed the build/tooling problem that FHIR-44992 resolved.
